_comment: Human-curated corrections, kept OUT of the scrapers so the line between what
Snow Peak published and what a person decided stays visible. build_catalog.py
applies these last and stamps span_source='curated'.
Every entry needs a `reason`. If a reason cannot be written, the part stays
unresolved -- an honest gap beats a confident guess.

XCK-128-01.title_en: Multi Function Table Rail Joint (2-piece set)
XCK-128-01.reason: The rail joint. Two come in the box with a bamboo corner, and it is sold on its own as a spare part. It is in NONE of the six IGT collections and its JP category is not IGT, so both halves of the universe miss it -- a catalog built from the vendor's taxonomy has holes exactly where the taxonomy has them. CK-119TR's manual, step 4: 'レールジョイントを使用する場合はIGTフレームの長辺のレールに挿入します' -- insert them into the rail on the frame's LONG SIDE -- then (5) hook the tabletop onto them. This is what makes the frame's long side attachable at all, and no product page or photograph says it exists.

CK-175.reason: IGTコネクションフック -- what joins two frames END TO END. A frame's end already has the HOLES (measured on CK-149: x = +/-406.5, z = +/-143.9); CK-175 supplies the other half by turning the neighbouring end into a HOOK. It is JP-only, has no manual, and exactly ONE real photograph in its gallery -- which happens to be of exactly this: two frames butted end to end, black end pieces face to face, two knurled thumbscrews spanning the joint, and TWO PAIRS OF LEGS bunched at it (so the frames do not share legs; each keeps its own four). The JP spec table says セット内容 本体×2 and 45g(本体一つあたり) -- a pair, 45g EACH -- so one set makes one joint (one hook per hole) and the SET weighs 90g. The scraper took the 45 as the item weight, which is what the page literally says and is not what it means.

CK-218.reason: ATTACH: the copy never says how the angle extensions attach, and their plan view shows the hooks only if you look for them on the SLANTED edge -- which the detector could not, because it tested for protrusion past the BOUNDING BOX. Two sources settle it. LV-381's manual, in English: 'it is possible to connect this product with a Bamboo IGT Table Regular / Long, Bamboo Left/Right Angle Extension, Bamboo Left / Right Corner Extension (CK-117TR, CK-218, CK-219, CK-118TR, CK-119TR)'. And the owner pointed at the hooks in the top view and at the close-up (JP a009): the same stainless wire hook, let into a slot in the board's edge, arching out and bending straight down. DEPTH: Snow Peak publishes 990x496, but that aspect (1.996) contradicts its own photograph (2.13) by 7% -- on BOTH mirror products, from two independent shots, while CK-117TR and CK-119TR agree with theirs to 0.6% and 0.3%. The hook spacing settles which number is wrong: it must match the frame's end holes (287.8mm), and it is 288-292mm on every other bamboo board. At the published scale CK-218's hooks come out 304mm apart -- a 5% outlier that would not enter the holes. At 990x465 they come out 289mm, the scale is isotropic (1.3866 vs 1.3881 mm/px), and the published WIDTH is reproduced to 0.4%. So 990 is real and 496 is not the bounding box; what Snow Peak means by it, I do not know, and am not going to invent. This matters because the ANGLE is measured in this frame: at the published scale the leg reads 61.2deg (turn 57.6), and at the true one 59.7deg (TURN 60.0).

CK-219.reason: Mirror of CK-218; same evidence and the same 6.4% aspect discrepancy in its own photograph, independently shot. Measured turn: 60.6deg.

GS-450R.reason: Along-rail 270mm against a 250mm unit. The extra 20mm is the rim resting on the rails, the way any drop-in cooktop overlaps its cutout -- the burner body drops through one unit. Snow Peak's own copy says only 'compatible with the Iron Grill Table System' and never states a count.

GS-230.reason: Along-rail 563mm against two units (500mm), same rim logic as GS-450R. Corroborated by the product copy: 'Pair the Double Burner Stove with the IGT 4 Unit Standing Set and the Double Bamboo Insert' -- the double insert takes 2 units, so the stove takes the remaining 2.

S-029HA.reason: Not an IGT part. It is a Takibi Fire & Grill accessory that the US storefront files under `cookers`. Its 'half-unit size' copy refers to the Takibi grill, not an IGT unit -- measured along-rail is 206mm against a 125mm half unit, which the fit cross-check flagged at +81mm.

S-029HD.reason: Same as S-029HA. Its own description says 'Use the Grill Plate Half Deep Depth within the Takibi Fire & Grill'.

GS-1000.reason: Round stove (JP size is written as a diameter, φ350x420). It does not sit in the grid on its own -- it mounts via the GP-040 joint frame, which is the part that occupies units.

CK-090.reason: Not an extension piece — it is a table in its own right. The copy: 'The Extension IGT is a two-unit expandable Iron Grill Table... does not require any connection tools or extension pieces... two laminated bamboo tabletops and an aluminum alloy stand.' JP size gives it away too: 1348×498×400(h)mm at 11kg, with its own legs. It stands at 400mm — the Layout System datum — so it joins the system as a node, not as a part bolted to a frame.

UG-472.reason: Snow Peak's own spec string is malformed: '(H)220x(W)360x(W)250mm' labels two axes W and none D. It is the same body as UG-471 ((H)110x(W)360x(D)250) at double height -- 110/220 in the names are the heights -- so the trailing 250 is the depth, one full unit along the rail.

GP-040.reason: UNRESOLVED on purpose. The JP name is 'IGT剛炎ジョイントフレーム' (joint frame) at 362x377mm, which is neither 250 (1 unit) nor 375 (1.5 units) cleanly. It is the mount that holds the GS-1000 in a frame, so it does occupy units, but the count is not derivable from any published number. Needs the manual PDF or a physical measurement.
